file-list.description: File paths with optional Git status, opaque datum keys, and the path currently displayed by a file viewer.

measured-scalar.description: The latest scalar emitted by a repeatable measurement source. Authored lf-num text freezes the value a version states; the source snapshot records whether that measurement ran again.

text-document.description: UTF-8 text from a file or a selected line range.

lf-ask.description: A question for the user. Around other widgets that ask for input it gives their heading and context, each widget answered separately; with no other widget inside, it is itself a question the user answers in words.
lf-ask.x-instructions: Around widgets that ask for input, give it a heading that states the shared question or context without leaning on the prose around it, with any eyebrow beside it in an `<hgroup>`. Each widget inside that asks for input stays its own obligation with its own answer, and the frame asks nothing itself. With no other widget inside, it is itself a question answered in words: in a reply's markup, by the user's next message in that thread; on the page, by their comment on it. Write the question itself as its content, with no heading needed. Wrap the context in a `section` when the document needs a section landmark.

What should a full store do?

The beta never reached the cap. This decides what the first workspace at it sees; each option draws its document list once the store fills. I recommend dropping the oldest documents, because editing continues and the server keeps a copy of each one.

editing: continuesrecommendedDrop the oldest documents Editing continues; the server keeps a copy. editing: pausedPause offline editing Nothing leaves.

lf-gloss.description: A short explanation the reader can open beside a phrase without leaving its sentence.
lf-gloss.x-instructions: Write a self-contained explanation at the first useful occurrence rather than on every repetition. Keep the phrase out of authored parentheses: print adds the explanation as a parenthetical note.

lf-num.description: A measured number in prose, tied to the data run that produced it.
lf-num.x-instructions: Write the value with its unit as the element's text. Bind `source` to the feed that measures it, and set `run` to the receipt `leaf data set` returned. Add `via` when the source id doesn't say which command or query produced it.
lf-num.x-example: The import now takes <lf-num source="import-latency" run="a41f103e236c985b" via="uv run bench-import">184 ms</lf-num> at p95.

lf-text-document.description: A text file from page data with numbered lines, syntax coloring, and an optional Markdown or HTML preview.
lf-text-document.x-instructions: Bind `source` to the page's data source and name the file with `label`. Set `preview` to `markdown` or `html` to add Preview and Source tabs over the same text. `language` colors the source, and defaults to the preview's language. An HTML preview is a separate document that inherits no Leaf styles, and comments can't reach inside it, so the user comments on the source. The listing, or with a preview each tab, scrolls inside a box `--lf-bound` tall, 28rem by default, however long the text. To start it collapsed, put it inside `details`.

lf-toc.description: An outline of the document’s h2–h6 headings for navigating its sections and showing the reader’s position.
lf-toc.x-instructions: Write it empty with a stable id. It outlines the nearest tab or part containing it, or the whole main when outside those views. Add `open` to show its compact inline links on arrival; the reader can still collapse them. Set `max-level` to leave out deeper headings that are local detail; by default it lists h2 to h6.

lf-activity.description: A newest-first feed of the page’s comments, actions, reports, and published revisions.
lf-activity.x-instructions: Write it empty with a stable id.

lf-options.description: Alternatives the user can choose individually or as a set to answer a question.
lf-options.x-instructions: Keep shared premises and evidence with the group (lf-ask can frame its question and context), and each alternative's own case and picture inside its lf-option. `multiple` lets the user pick several options as one answer (references/authoring-on-me.md says when). The built-in Another option field takes unlisted answers, so add no catch-all option. Use `for` only to point at sections or work items that exist apart from the question. A `multiple` group needs the user's Done even when `chosen` is authored. `settled` collapses a decided group while keeping its options and anchors.
lf-options.x-example:
Where should run status appear?

Both choices preserve the existing run detail.

effort: lowrisk: medrecommended Status on the run list One join; failures are visible without a click. effort: nonerisk: low Leave the list alone No work; failures stay one click away.

lf-option.description: One alternative in a decision: a compact label, or a card showing what choosing it gives the user.
lf-option.x-instructions: Word, label and illustrate the alternatives as `references/authoring-on-me.md` says. A card opens with its small.tag labels, then `<small class="tag ok">recommended</small>` on the option you advise, then a `<strong>` title and a sentence naming its consequence, then any picture as block HTML, such as an svg.drawing. Give your reason for the recommendation in prose beside the group, such as the `lf-ask`'s paragraph, so each card states only what choosing it does. Direct text takes inline Markdown. `chosen` records the user's pick. Use `$restated` to withdraw that pick and ask again. A `for` target must stay useful whatever is decided, and does not supply the option's words. `value` names what the option answers wherever a view shows the group's answer, such as a board column (`authoring-on-me.md`, "One decision in its section and on a board").

lf-code.description: A source-code excerpt with syntax coloring, highlighted lines, and line-anchored remarks.
lf-code.x-instructions: Write the exact code inside pre at column 0, HTML-escaping & before < and >. Set language for source code and omit it for plain transcripts or command output. For excerpts, set lines to the ascending source ranges quoted, such as 1505-1507,1520-1527; hi and lf-note at then use those source numbers. A note addressed to an omitted line captions the elided row.
lf-code.x-example:
def bracket(temp):
    if temp < 0:
        return "steel"
    return "cedar"
Freezing is the only threshold that matters.

lf-note.description: A prose remark anchored to a line or omitted range of its lf-code parent.
lf-note.x-instructions: Set at to the line number as the parent numbers it: 1-based by default, or the source number declared in lines.

lf-chart.description: An Observable Plot chart authored with Plot’s API and sized to its place in the page.
lf-chart.x-instructions: Inside a `<pre>`, write a JavaScript expression for the options object you would pass to `Plot.plot`, HTML-escaping & before < and >. `Plot` and `width` are the names in scope, and the data goes inline. The chart requires an `ariaLabel` describing it. Leave `width` and `height` out of the options: read `width` to fit the ticks to the room, and set a height other than the default with `data-height` on the element. Write dates as ISO strings on an explicitly typed time scale, `utc` for days and months, and give moments a time zone, such as 2026-06-01T14:00Z. Use `var(--series-N)` for constant or categorical colors; a continuous color scale needs a Plot scheme. Title the chart in the heading or prose around it rather than with Plot's `title`. When `page check --render` reports overlapping labels, use fewer category ticks, choose them by `width`, or give the axis label more margin. Plot takes a mark's `dx`, `dy` and `textAnchor` as one value for the whole mark, so labels that each need their own offset, such as line ends that meet, each take a mark of their own.
lf-chart.x-example:
{
  ariaLabel: "Hours to first review by week: backend fell from 31 to 12, frontend from 18 to 11",
  x: {type: "utc", ticks: "monday", label: null},
  y: {grid: true, label: "hours to first review"},
  color: {legend: true, range: ["var(--series-1)", "var(--series-2)"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.lineY(
      [
        {week: "2026-05-04", team: "backend", hours: 31},
        {week: "2026-05-11", team: "backend", hours: 26},
        {week: "2026-05-18", team: "backend", hours: 12},
        {week: "2026-05-04", team: "frontend", hours: 18},
        {week: "2026-05-11", team: "frontend", hours: 21},
        {week: "2026-05-18", team: "frontend", hours: 11},
      ],
      {x: "week", y: "hours", stroke: "team", marker: true},
    ),
  ],
}

lf-shot.description: A before-and-after pair of screenshots with paired, slider and pixel-difference views, change outlines and scale controls.
lf-shot.x-instructions: Use it for two versions of an interface. Set `before` and `after` to the paths `leaf page media` prints, and describe the pair in `alt`. `authoring-evidence.md`, "Source files and media", covers making captures, laying out captures that vary along more than one axis in a table, and the comparison controls the reader can use. Put explanation in the prose around the pair, not inside the element. When a decision turns on the change, put the pair inside the option that proposes it, or, for an accept-or-reject decision, with the group, where it shows both answers.

The chips now sit above the title, so a scanning eye reads cost before prose.

lf-board.description: Cards grouped into columns for scanning work and status, with movement and reordering available.
lf-board.x-instructions: Use a board to show grouped work and status. When the user must make decisions, give them explicit controls or `lf-options` rather than relying on moving cards, and to gather those answers on a board as well, give each card `shows`. When revising, keep each card the user moved in the column they chose, unless the revision retracts that move by marking the card, not the board, `restated` (`authoring-revisions.md`, "Honor user state").

lf-column.description: One named board column, including empty columns the user can move a card into.
lf-column.x-instructions: Write a label that names the column on its own. Use tone when landing here carries a status judgment, such as blocked, needing review, or done; otherwise leave it neutral. On a board whose cards show answers, `value` names the answer the column holds, and a column without one holds the answers that name none.

lf-card.description: One board card whose identity and comments survive user moves.
lf-card.x-instructions: Lead with a `<strong>` title and follow with prose. Keep its id stable across moves. Use `$restated` to withdraw the user's moves. `shows` makes the card a view of a decision widget's answer: it stands in the column whose `value` that answer names, and moving it changes the answer (`authoring-on-me.md`, "One decision in its section and on a board").

lf-tabs.description: Several views shown one at a time: page navigation, a tabbed box, or a queue beside its open item.
lf-tabs.x-instructions: The first `lf-tabs` written directly in `main` is the page's navigation; any other tab set is a framed box within the page. Put the page's title and lede before page tabs, and the main current view first. Make each `lf-tab` a self-contained view; history, threads and versions belong to the whole page. When current work no longer needs a view, remove it. Move any context still needed, and any passage an open thread or an unretracted decision is anchored to, into a `details` in the relevant tab. Use `list="side"` for a queue listed beside the item it opens.

lf-tally.description: A count of the open obligations in one region, such as the decisions left in a queue, split into those waiting on the user and those waiting on the agent, with an optional control that goes to the next one waiting on the user.
lf-tally.x-instructions: Write it empty with a stable id, and set `for` to the region whose obligations it counts, such as a side-list `lf-tabs` queue. Place it where the reader looks for the queue's state, such as a workspace header beside its `.tag` chips. Add `next` for a Next on me control that steps through the obligations waiting on the user.

lf-tab.description: One labeled view in a tab set, optionally summarized and grouped in a side-list queue.
lf-tab.x-instructions: In a side-list queue, write each tab's `summary` and `group` as `page-layout.md`, "A workspace", says. Keep ids distinct across tabs, which share the page's id space.

lf-parts.description: A page made of parts, each laid out by a Layout of its own and shown one at a time, listed down the window's left edge under the page's title.
lf-parts.x-instructions: Place it as `page-layout.md`, "A page of parts", says, giving each `lf-part` one child carrying that part's Layout, such as `<article class="layout-column">`. Put the main current part first. History, threads and versions belong to the whole page. When current work no longer needs a part, remove it, moving any passage an open thread or an unretracted decision is anchored to into a `details` in the relevant part.

lf-part.description: One labeled part of a page, holding the box its own Layout arranges.
lf-part.x-instructions: Hold exactly one child, carrying the part's Layout. Its `summary` shows under its label in the list, so the user can tell the parts apart before opening one; start it with what the part holds unless the label already says so. Keep ids distinct across parts, which share the page's id space.

lf-draft.description: A block of text the user owns and can rewrite in place, with recorded revision history.
lf-draft.x-instructions:
Write the exact Markdown source as `
`, one newline, the HTML-escaped source (& before < and >), then `
` right after it. HTML drops that first newline; every later character, indentation and trailing newlines included, is part of the draft. With `needed`, a draft asks the user for an edit; without it, it is an optional editing surface. Use lf-ask when the request needs its own heading and evidence, or an lf-options decision for permission to use the finished wording. Keep the user's exact source on revision (authoring-revisions.md, "Honor user state"); to replace an edited passage on purpose, write the new text and mark the draft `restated` ($restated).

lf-sample.description: A labeled sample: quoted content, interactive content on this page, or an isolated child Leaf page.
lf-sample.x-instructions: Use interactive for inline controls that share this page’s state and Undo. For an isolated live child page, put its main content in one direct template[data-sample] with a stable id. Use window for a whole Leaf window including its chrome. Read live-samples.md for child-page interaction, reset, and isolation.

lf-pane.description: A reading region with an optional header and footer, independently scrollable inside a full-height workspace.
lf-pane.x-instructions: For independent scrolling, place the pane as a full-height workspace’s body or a direct cell; elsewhere the page scrolls. Wrap multiple body blocks in one div or section. Use label to name the region accessibly and its header for the visible heading. Put action widgets in the direct footer when they should remain reachable as the body scrolls.
